Theme

Town, shops & places · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

area noun

a part of a place: a region, a neighbourhood

also region, district, parts, around here, in this area, section of a city, zone

classical

Liv. 1.4.6: in hīs locīs
Cic. Att. 15.16a: haec loca venusta sunt

loca, locōrum n. pl.

noun, second declension, plural

parts, a region, an area

The plural of locus for a stretch of country: in hīs locīs, in these parts, in this area.

Other words

  • regiō, regiōnis f. — a region, a district

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Liv. 22.46.9: regiōnis incolae, the people of the area; Plin. NH 3.46: discrīptiōnemque ab eō factam Ītaliae tōtīus in regiōnēs XI; Traupman 206: region; Traupman 124

    The word for a larger region, and for an administrative one: Augustus divided Italy into eleven regiōnēs (Plin. NH 3.46) and Rome into fourteen (Plin. NH 3.66).

  • vīcīnia, vīcīniae f. — the neighbourhood: round here

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 95: hīc vīcīniae; Ter. And. 70: hūc vīcīniae

    Terence’s genitive of place: hīc vīcīniae, here in the neighbourhood.

  • zōna, zōnae f. — a zone of the earth; classically also a girdle

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Verg. G. 1.233 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. time zone: zōna temporālis (after Egger)

    Greek ζώνη, a girdle; classically one of the five belts into which the earth was divided, from torrid to frozen (Lewis & Short). For a zone in a town or on a map (a pedestrian zone, a danger zone) regiō or loca says it in classical Latin.

  • ārea, āreae f. — an open space: a yard, a building plot, a threshing floor

    noun, first declension · avoid · classical · Dig. 50.16.211: locus sine aedificiō in urbe ārea (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. square, piazza; s.v. yard

    A false friend: never a region. Traupman’s ārea portāria and ārea poenālis, the goal and penalty areas (Traupman 50), keep the classical sense of a marked-out open space.

Examples

  • vāstae tum in hīs locīs sōlitūdinēs erant

    in those days this whole area was wildernessLiv. 1.4.6

  • modo quandam vīdī virginem hīc vīcīniae

    just now I saw a girl here in the neighbourhoodTer. Ph. 95

  • in Lūsitāniā ad ōceanum in eā regiōne, ubi est oppidum Olisīpō, monte Tagrō quaedam ē ventō concipiunt certō tempore equae

    in Lusitania by the ocean, in the region where the town of Olisipo lies, on Mount Tagrus, some mares conceive from the wind at a certain seasonVarr. RR 2.1.19

See also community, neighbour, village, town.
